reading.body:
CyrusOne's SAT1 campus in San Antonio publishes 9 MW of IT capacity, one of only 19 Texas data centers that disclose a power figure at all.

Texas has 133 mapped facilities, and the state's 475 MW of disclosed IT load is a floor rather than a total. SAT1 holds 1.9% of that disclosed load and ranks 14th in the state, so its position reflects who reports as much as who builds. Texas trails only California and Virginia on disclosed capacity, which is a statement about reporting as well as construction.

For AI specifically, 9 MW is small to mid-size. At 40 kW per rack, an assumption rather than a measurement, the 110,000 square feet of technical space works out to roughly 225 racks. That is not a frontier training cluster. The certifications, HIPAA, PCI DSS, FISMA, ISO 27001, SSAE 16 Type II and TIA-942, describe a facility built for regulated financial and government workloads rather than for the largest distributed training runs.

The data does not cover backup power, renewable sourcing, grid connection, or any announced expansion. The suitability score of 56 is derived only from published IT capacity and operator type, and it names announced expansion as the missing input. Nothing here indicates how much additional power the site could draw, which is the fact that would determine whether it grows.

suitability.basis: weighted mean of the published inputs named here, scaled to 100; formula on the methodology page
